name: perishable_heterogeneous
label_authority: Elicit run of 20 Oct 2026 as saved. The Close / Adjacent / Methodological strata are the tool's own match labels from abstracts; no human verification.
identity_rule: DOI or verified work identity; title-only matches require adjudication
question: Allocation of perishable resources among heterogeneous demand classes with different service success probabilities or rates, accounting for resource age, expiration, long-run service requirements and allocation costs.
reference: Elicit answer, 20 Oct 2026, saved in notes/test-questions/perishable-resource-heterogeneous-classes/. A broader, more formal version of perishable_two_classes, asked the same day. Elicit reports 88 indexed papers and delivers 12.
expected_direction: No exact match to the full formulation was confirmed, stated openly, in particular the combination of class-specific success probabilities conditional on allocation with minimum long-run service requirements. Closest: Abouee-Mehrizi 2019 and Chen 2018 for age-sensitive multiclass allocation, Civelek 2015 for protection levels with allocation costs in an infinite horizon, Bar-Lev 2005 for expiration with urgency classes and steady-state unsatisfied demand. Allocation Policies in Blood Transfusion links inventory-age distributions to adverse-outcome probabilities and is adjacent evidence only. Freshness eligibility, fill rates and processing speed are kept apart, not treated as interchangeable.

answer_elements.question: Close age-sensitive multiclass allocation models, with the rationing rule from a located passage
Allocation costs and protection levels over an infinite horizon
Expiration with urgency classes and steady-state service measures
Age-dependent outcome probability, used as adjacent evidence and not as a match
Separation of freshness eligibility, fill rate or service level, processing rate and conditional success probability, with no exact match confirmed and no novelty claimed from absence

pass_rule.status: draft from QUESTION.md, owner has not confirmed it
rules: At least the three papers named in Elicit's answer (Abouee-Mehrizi 2019, Civelek 2015, Bar-Lev 2005) are found.
Answer keeps freshness eligibility, fill rate/service level, processing rate and conditional success probability separate, and says no exact match was confirmed.
Blood-transfusion paper is used for age-to-outcome probability only, not as a match.
Absence of an exact match is not turned into a novelty claim.
